facts.text: Evidence is a recorded fact, such as a test result, measurement, field record, analysis or document, that supports or weakens a claim; its strength depends on its producer, independence and direct relevance to the claim.
facts.quote: Evidence is any recorded fact (a test result, a measurement, a field record, an analysis, a document) that supports or weakens a claim, and its strength depends on who produced it, how independently, and how directly it bears on the claim.

facts.text: An independent measurement of the real thing is the strongest engineering evidence.
facts.quote: An independent measurement of the real thing is strongest.

facts.text: A supplier's claim about its own product is weaker evidence than an independent measurement because the supplier has a stake in the outcome; expert opinion without data is weaker still.
facts.quote: A supplier's claim about its own product is weaker, because the supplier has a stake. An expert's opinion without data is weaker still.

facts.text: Evidence from a similar but different setting, such as road cars standing in for haul trucks, is weaker than direct evidence.
facts.quote: Evidence from a similar but different setting (road cars standing in for haul trucks) is weaker than direct evidence.

facts.text: A blind prediction that proved correct is stronger evidence than a model tuned after the fact.
facts.quote: A blind prediction that proved right is stronger than a model tuned after the fact.

facts.text: Independent evidence must be produced by people with no stake in the outcome and based on data not used to build or tune the system being judged.
facts.quote: Independent means two things: produced by people with no stake in the outcome, and based on data not used to build or tune the thing being judged.

facts.text: The booklet recommends keeping verified fact, expert judgment and management assumption in three categories that are never mixed.
facts.quote: keep verified fact, expert judgment and management assumption in three categories that are never mixed

facts.text: The program should build an evidence ledger mapping each sub-claim to its evidence item, method, credibility level and acceptance criterion.
facts.quote: build an evidence ledger mapping each sub-claim to its evidence item, method, credibility level and acceptance criterion [Chapter 12]

facts.text: Every reviewer should receive a one-page claim map identifying whether each claim's evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, the real data used to validate the underlying model, and who accepts the remaining uncertainty.
facts.quote: give every reviewer a one-page map showing, for each claim, whether its evidence is virtual, physical or mixed, what real data validated the model behind it, and who accepts the remaining uncertainty [Chapter 13]

facts.text: A mining company's history of installing systems on the basis of supplier claims and subsequently experiencing field failures provides a warning about vendor evidence.
facts.quote: A mining company's history of systems installed on supplier claims that then failed in the field is the warning about vendor evidence [Chapter 13].

facts.text: Simulation provides evidence of coverage and design correctness.
facts.quote: Simulation is evidence of coverage and design correctness

facts.text: Correlated physical tests provide evidence that a simulation represents the real machine.
facts.quote: correlated physical tests are evidence that the simulation represents the real machine

facts.text: Prescribed physical tests must remain physical rather than being replaced with simulation.
Virtual results count as evidence only inside a validated envelope, anchored by independent physical tests and approved as specific substitutions rather than as blanket approval of virtual testing.
facts.quote: yes, inside a validated envelope, anchored by independent physical tests, and approved as specific substitutions rather than as "virtual testing" in general [Chapters 3, 10, 13].
